common_misconceptions: Assuming that an atypical or mild presentation rules out Acute dacryocystitis (lacrimal sac abscess).
Relying solely on a single normal laboratory value or imaging result to prematurely exclude pathology.
Equating temporary symptomatic relief with full resolution of the underlying condition without completing standard evaluation.
Misattributing symptoms exclusively to Preseptal cellulitis without completing a comprehensive diagnostic workup.
dangerous_errors: Failing to recognize red-flag features and delaying urgent escalation or emergency intervention.
Prematurely discharging or reassuring the patient before completing appropriate diagnostic assessment.
Initiating empirical treatment without considering major patient contraindications or drug interactions.
Ignoring critical warning signs such as: Spread to orbital cellulitis if untreated.

must_ask.say: Can you show me exactly where the swelling and tenderness are?

must_ask.objective: Ask about discharge from the tear duct area
must_ask.say: Have you noticed pus or discharge from near your tear duct?
Have you had excessive tearing or a blocked tear duct before this started?

must_ask.objective: Screen for fever or spreading redness
must_ask.say: Do you have a fever, spreading redness, any change in vision, or pain when moving the eye?
